title: iOS 27 Simulator on x86-64 Linux
summary: Apple's arm64-only iOS 27 Simulator runtime, unmodified, translated to x86-64 on the fly by an embedded JIT (dynarmic) inside Darling. No Mac at runtime. Graphics, input and networking go to native Linux services.
now: Speed 12: the keyboard works (InputUI + assistantd jobs; simhid attaches its keyboard on the first key, so text fields show the software keyboard; typing on it works in Settings search). Calendar, Photos and Maps open cold in 4-6 / 4-6 / 9-13 s and warm in 2 s. A Darling RPC bug (msg_controllen not restored before re-receiving, so an S2C mmap lost its FD) aborted backboardd and then darlingserver on app launches: fixed. Photos needs assetsd (zeroed allocations: Apple's lexicon store relies on zero-on-free). AOT image retrained on SpringBoard after home, Settings sub-pages and search, the keyboard, and the three apps: 1.98M blocks, uncovered JIT code after the apps 306 -> 139 MB; shared code cache 768 MB. Home 24-33 s, Settings 11 s cold / 4 s warm, PSS 2.41-2.42 GB (43 procs: InputUI, assistantd and the daemons it pulls in, +267 MB), 3 consecutive clean boots + apps. Speed 11: home 29-32 -> 20/20/24 s, PSS 2.29 -> 2.15-2.16 GB for one sim (anon without mtlvk 674-680 -> 597-604 MB). iconservicesagent wiped its icon store, and with it the Metal shader cache IconServices keeps there, at every launch: it keeps the store only if the directory's owner is _iconservices. So every boot re-rendered every icon, and MTLCompilerService spent 11.9 CPU-s compiling RenderBox pipelines, which also held SpringBoard's main queue on a FrontBoard lock for ~4.5 s. The arm64 simshim now reports _iconservices for our own files in that daemon only, so MTLCompilerService no longer starts on a warm boot. Apple's 125/3 guest timebase is now the default: the Speed 10 spin was libdispatch timer re-arms handed back from the workqueue callbacks unconverted. Boots prefetch the last boot's hot dyld-cache and image pages: with an evicted page cache, home 57-60 s -> 30-52 s. dynarmic maps run at 0.9 load: SpringBoard -11 MB. Settings cold 10 s / warm 3 s, 3 consecutive clean boots, idle <=1%. Speed 10: home 42 -> 29-32 s (AOT image fast load: every process parsed the 1.2M-entry index under a lock), memory 2.40 -> 2.29 GB PSS for one sim (anon without mtlvk 769 -> 674-680 MB: lf_map at 75% load, adaptive guest-heap refill, image trained on every daemon), fresh second instances via A64_CLONE_FROM reach home in 25 s (was ~5 min with a SpringBoard relaunch on the LaunchServices build), Apple's 125/3 guest timebase implemented behind X86CODE_A64_TIMEBASE=apple (Swift sleeps right without the patch; a Darling workqueue spin keeps it off). Settings cold 9 s / warm 3 s, 3 consecutive clean boots. Speed 9: Swift sleeps fixed (libswift_Concurrency inlined Apple-silicon timebase: every Task.sleep fired at once; Preferences idle 90% -> 0% CPU, 10k -> 2 wakeups/s), GetBlock FastDispatch probe on by default (its Speed 7/8 crashes were a torn 16-byte read), metalhostd NULL-context guard and back on the image, shared prelude (-46 MB anon), no 6.5 GB of .bin autosaves per boot, fresh devices without blank widget tiles. Home 42 s, Settings cold 9-12 s / warm 3 s, 3 consecutive clean boots. Settings search 'Time' overlap is iOS 27 Liquid Glass (matches Xcode's simulator). Speed 8: memory 2.74 -> 2.32 GB PSS for one sim (38 procs); second instance boots side by side (shared mtlvk, private /dev/shm): two instances 3.27 GB, marginal ~0.93 GB. Home 36 s, Settings cold 12 s / warm 3 s, zero crashes. Speed 7: memory 3.92 -> 2.70 GB PSS (SpringBoard 748->~490, Preferences 596->~300, backboardd 466->~135, daemons ~65->~28 MB each); home 37 s, Settings cold 10-16 s / warm 2-3 s, zero crashes. Speed 5: crash elimination. Cold boot + Settings + 4 reopens with zero process crashes/restarts (was ~245 s with 3 SpringBoard restarts). Fixed: UI-sensor abort, objc cache UAF + bucket race, 16K-page unmaps spilling into stub images/neighbours, hanging fault handler, AOT image fault, saver thread aborting metalhostd. Persistent JIT cache now autosaves; linked AOT image loaded by backboardd/SpringBoard/Preferences by default.

stages.name: 0. Proof of concept
stages.detail: Small arm64 iOS-simulator programs run on x86-64 Linux under dynarmic. 2.45x slower than native x86 overall; calls into native x86 code cost nothing.

stages.name: 1. Inside Darling
stages.detail: Darling's loader hands arm64 programs to the JIT. Apple's own dyld_sim maps the iOS 27 shared cache; libobjc and libswiftCore run translated. System calls go through native x86 libsystem stubs generated from the cache.

stages.name: 2. Boot to the home screen
stages.detail: launchd_sim → daemons → backboardd → SpringBoard, all arm64 under the JIT, software rendering. Fixed: native malloc, signal delivery, per-thread data, tagged pointers, FP16 instructions, thread cleanup, memory-range exhaustion.

stages.name: 3. Fast and lean
stages.detail: Done: shared cache, slim-park, idle CPU, Metal CA home+Settings, openurl/nsurlsessiond, launch breakdown, svc objc_msgSend experiment (opt-in; inlined next). Next: persistent JIT cache, inlined objc_msgSend, Preferences spin, AOT. Speed 3: inline objc_msgSend and a persistent JIT cache are on; boot 71 s, Settings reopen 5 s.

stages.name: 4. Near native
stages.detail: Translate ahead of time, like Rosetta 2, with the JIT as fallback. (1) iOS system libraries: the code that actually runs is recorded and translated once per iOS version. (2) That translation is shared read-only by every iOS process instead of each keeping its own copy: the main lever for under 1 GB per app. (3) Apps are translated when installed, then refined from what runs. (4) Anything missed, or generated at run time (JavaScript JIT), still goes through the JIT and is saved for next time. ASLR is off for the sim's processes only, so translations stay valid.

speed7.home_s: 37-38 (56 on the first boot after an image rebuild)
speed7.notes: Lazy AOT metadata in a shared static index; every ASLR-off process maps the shared image (daemons ~65->~28 MB); 64K FastDispatch for daemons; native Swift conformance step (conformance 14.5%->3.5% of Preferences cold CPU). Open: Settings search 'Time' placeholder crossfade.

speed9.notes: Swift timebase patch (X86CODE_A64_SWIFT_TIMEBASE), GetBlock FD probe default (X86CODE_A64_GETBLOCK_FD=0 off), metalhostd guard + on image, prelude sharing (X86CODE_A64_PRELUDE_SHARE), launchd_sim off the image, no .bin autosave with the image (X86CODE_A64_AOT_AUTOSAVE=1 for training), fresh-device IconState seed. Lookups (accounts/followup/profiled) measured: not a boot cost, not stubbed.

speed10.notes: AOT image fast load (map the published .idx: ~300 ms serialized per process -> 1-2 ms), boot-inner cgroup scan without ~35k forks, lf_map 75% load, adaptive gheap refill, image trained on every daemon (25 profiles), A64_CLONE_FROM for fresh devices (home 25 s instead of ~5 min with a SpringBoard relaunch), X86CODE_A64_TIMEBASE=apple (125/3 at the thunks; off: Darling's workqueue manager spins in 8 processes), sampler fixes (GSAMPLE_OUT/ALL). Boot is latency-bound (host ~80% idle); remaining: MTLCompilerService recompiles shaders every boot (11.9 CPU-s), host page-cache misses.

speed11.home_s: 20/20/24 (fin4-6; Speed 10 29/29/32; 26 s on the icon fix alone)
speed11.notes: Icon store (and its __METAL_CACHE__) kept across boots: simshim fileOwnerAccountName=_iconservices in iconservicesagent; MTLCompilerService not started on warm boots; the SpringBoard FrontBoard lock wait went with it. X86CODE_A64_TIMEBASE defaults to apple (=1to1 old mode): the workqueue kevent/workloop callbacks return timer changes that Darling's native libpthread passes to __workq_kernreturn, now converted. boot-a64 prefetch (A64_PREFETCH=0 off). dynarmic block_descriptors/patch heads at 0.9 load. Darling kevent manager event log behind /private/var/tmp/x86code-wqdbg.

speed12.notes: InputUI, assistantd, assetsd jobs; simhid keyboard on first key; Darling dserver RPC msg_controllen fix (libsystem_kernel in the arm64 prefix only); assetsd MallocZeroOnAlloc; image 1.98M blocks (530 MB, 63 profiles); code cache 768 MB. Icon store seeding for fresh devices tried and reverted (store UUID follows each device's LaunchServices DB).
